findings.description: The Lambda function's environment variables embed a long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE / wJalrXUtnFEMI...). Any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can read these, and they are also stored in Terraform state, so the credentials should be supplied via AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store with a KMS-encrypted key.

findings.issue_category: missing KMS encryption for environment variables
findings.description: No kms_key_arn is set on the function, so the environment block holding the static AWS keys is encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and is readable by any role permitted lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. An explicit customer-managed KMS key would restrict decryption rights to the intended principals.

runtime = "nodejs12.x" is an EOL, unpatched runtime that no longer receives security fixes, leaving the function exposed to known Node.js vulnerabilities. This should be upgraded to a currently supported runtime.

The Lambda execution role has no permissions_boundary and no explicit policy attached, so its effective privileges depend entirely on separately managed policies and are unconstrained by the stack. A permissions boundary should cap the maximum privileges the role can obtain.
